title: Weekly review
hook: look back on the week kindly; why the second day of creation is never called good, and what Rashi says about it
tomorrow: does a phone break the Sabbath? there's more than one answer.

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: longer silence. Elijah waited out the wind, the earthquake and the fire, and the still small voice came after. Today, the end of the week, and a look back.

Sunday night, and the weekly review turns into a list of everything that went wrong. Genesis has a stranger list. Read its first chapter slowly and a refrain keeps coming back: God saw that it was good. Day one, good. Day three, good, and then good again. Days four, five and six, good. But the second day, when the waters are split by the firmament, gets no good at all. The rabbis noticed. Why would the maker skip a day?
screen: `THE REVIEW BECOMES A LIST OF FAILURES.` → `GOD SAW THAT IT WAS GOOD.` → `DAY TWO: NO GOOD AT ALL.` → `WHY SKIP A DAY?`

segments.voice: Rashi, a medieval Jewish commentator on the Torah, gives an answer. On the second day, the work of the waters wasn't finished. God divided them, but they weren't gathered into seas until the third day. And something unfinished isn't called good yet. So the third day gets the word twice: once for its own work, and once for finishing the second. Then, at the end of the sixth day, comes a look over everything: "And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good." And on the seventh day, rest. So Genesis gives the week a shape: six days of making, a look back, and a day of rest. The Sabbath commandment in Exodus points straight back to it, and the Jewish week still ends in Shabbat. And the look back in Genesis is generous. It doesn't pretend day two was done. It waits, and calls it good when the work is finished. That's a kind way to review a week. Some days were good. Some are still unfinished, and unfinished is different from bad. Their good may come on a later day. A review in this pattern isn't a trial. It's a walk back through seven days, saying good where you can, and not yet where you can't.
screen: `THE WATERS WEREN'T FINISHED.` · `UNFINISHED ISN'T CALLED GOOD YET.` · `DAY THREE: GOOD, TWICE.` · `VERY GOOD, THEN REST.` · then, large: `THE WEEK.`

segments.voice: Choose your review night, Friday or Sunday, and fix it in your calendar. Then try a small one now: name one day this week you'd call good, and one you'd call not finished yet. Say both gently, the way Genesis waits for day two.
Weekly review: a kind look back over seven days, saying good where you can, and not finished yet where you can't.
Pocket this one: the week, where even day two got its good in the end. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some people keep a weekly review on Friday afternoon or Sunday evening: a quiet half hour with a notebook, walking back through each day and noting what went well, what is unfinished and what comes next.
